source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #268 (branch fix/241-sort-value at head 5536558521eca906c8ba5b2613fed4f3c4ded378 — branch commits 5b404d4 (the #241 value index space) and 5536558 (the Codex P1 follow-up adding the ValueBudget decode budget) on current main 3e1d335, so the pull-request run built the same tree; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45138823545 and 45138835861 against the branch and pull-request run 45136051551, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #268 (#241, the component model value index space: Sort::Value, sort 0x02, value imports/exports). The PR implements the value index space end to end in telomere-component — decode, validation, instantiation and link-time resolution of value imports/exports, static literal decoding of the value section, and the linker’s register_import_value — and a follow-up commit answers a Codex P1 review finding: a list whose element type has an empty encoding decoded its element count without consuming any input bytes, so a 26-byte component could materialise billions of values and abort the embedding process on allocation; the value decoder now charges every node materialised without consuming input bytes against a zero-width ValueBudget and checks list element counts against the remaining encoding bytes plus that budget before any element is materialised. The branch is based on current main (3e1d335) with no merge, so the first CI run tripped the gate on the PR’s own change. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (3e1d335) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45138848073, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 32 gated series, so every delta is this PR’s own. The growth is confined to the three configurations that link the component runtime: component (release stripped file +50,568 B / stripped .text +44,720 B; release-size stripped file +28,664 B / stripped .text +25,024 B), wasi (release stripped file +48,056 B / stripped .text +42,640 B; release-size stripped file +28,856 B / stripped .text +25,216 B) and wasi-threads (release stripped file +48,040 B / stripped .text +42,640 B; release-size stripped file +28,824 B / stripped .text +25,200 B). The other 20 of the 32 gated series are byte-identical. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is now the release-size component stripped .text series at +5.05% (1,169,031 B to 1,228,023 B), up from +3.54% (release-size core-jit stripped .text, unchanged by this PR). Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (16 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3; the raw file and .text sizes were also identical across the three runs), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, ‘Size regression gate (#164)’.
